Perfume bottle insert trays are a precision cosmetics packaging application — the insert tray must hold the fragrance bottle in exact label-visible orientation within the gift box, protect the glass bottle from transit vibration without allowing glass-to-cavity contact that could cause surface damage, and maintain the bottle at the correct height within the gift box for the box window presentation. sections.st: Three Problems Perfume Bottle Insert Trays Buyers Face

strips.title: Glass Fragrance Bottles Vibrate Against Standard Cavity Walls
strips.desc: Problem: Standard thermoformed cavity walls that contact the glass bottle face during transit vibration cause surface micro-abrasion on the bottle face — invisible in static display but showing a fine haze pattern under cosmetics retail lighting. Solution: PETG cavity geometry with vibration damping clearance — the bottle is supported at the base and shoulder, with the glass face of the bottle having a calibrated clearance gap from the cavity wall.

strips.title: Bottle Not in Label-Visible Orientation in Gift Box
strips.desc: Problem: Perfume bottle insert trays where the bottle is not in exact label-visible orientation at the gift box window — the brand name and bottle face design are rotated away from the consumer's view. Solution: Label-visible orientation is confirmed from the physical perfume bottle before cavity design. Bottle orientation is locked by cavity geometry — the bottle can only insert in the label-visible position.

strips.title: Height Mismatch — Perfume Bottle Too Low or Too High for Gift Box Window
strips.desc: Problem: Fragrance gift set inserts where the bottle height in the tray does not align with the gift box window height — the bottle top appears too low or the cap protrudes above the box window opening. Solution: Box window height and bottle height confirmed before tray design — tray base height adjusted to position the bottle correctly at the box window.

sections.st: Perfume Bottle Insert Trays — Key Design Requirements

strips.title: Vibration Damping Clearance — Glass Bottle Face Must Not Contact Cavity
strips.desc: Glass fragrance bottle faces have applied labels, screenprinted decoration, or etched surfaces. Cavity wall contact during transit vibration causes surface abrasion on these finishes. PETG cavity geometry provides vibration damping clearance — the glass bottle face has a defined clearance gap from the cavity wall. Clearance tolerance confirmed from the bottle decoration specification.

strips.title: Label-Visible Orientation Lock — Cavity Prevents Incorrect Bottle Insertion
strips.desc: Perfume bottle cavity geometry is designed so the bottle can only be inserted in the correct label-visible orientation — cavity geometry matches the bottle profile only in the correct orientation. If the bottle is inserted incorrectly, it does not seat fully in the cavity. This prevents incorrect bottle orientation in the gift box at the packing stage.

strips.title: Gift Box Height Positioning — Tray Base Height Calculation
strips.desc: Tray base height is calculated from the gift box interior height, the gift box window position, and the fragrance bottle height — so the bottle is positioned at the correct height for the box window presentation. Confirmed from physical gift box and bottle before tooling.

strips.title: PETG for Luxury Fragrance Brands — Superior Clarity Communicates Luxury
strips.desc: Luxury and niche fragrance brands use PETG thermoforming for insert trays — the superior optical clarity of PETG does not compete visually with the fragrance bottle's premium design. A low-clarity insert detracts from the luxury bottle's visual impact.

faqs.q: Why is PETG preferred over APET for luxury fragrance inserts?
faqs.a: PETG provides superior optical clarity over APET — a visible difference at the retail shelf, with a premium surface finish that does not compete visually with the luxury fragrance bottle design. For niche and luxury fragrance brands, PETG communicates the correct premium tier. APET is the correct material for mid-range and mass-market fragrance packaging.

faqs.q: How is vibration damping achieved for glass fragrance bottles?
faqs.a: PETG cavity geometry with calibrated clearance — the glass bottle face has a defined clearance gap from the cavity wall, so bottle and cavity wall do not contact during transit vibration. The bottle is supported only at the structural base and shoulder. Clearance tolerance confirmed from the bottle decoration specification.

faqs.q: What is label-visible orientation lock in perfume insert design?
faqs.a: Cavity geometry designed to match the bottle profile only in the correct label-visible orientation — the bottle can only fully seat in the cavity when in the correct position. Prevents incorrect bottle orientation at the packing stage.
